UN R53.scope_evidence: This Regulation applies to vehicles of category L3 with regard to the installation of lighting and light-signalling devices.

UN R100.scope_evidence: Safety requirements with respect to the electric power train of road vehicles of categories M, N and O1 ... equipped with electric power train

UN R101.scope_evidence: applies to vehicles of categories M1 and N1 with regard to: (a) the measurement of the emission of carbon dioxide (CO2) and fuel consumption and/or ... electric energy consumption and electric range
UN R101.reason: UN R101 approves whole vehicles for measured CO2 emissions, fuel and energy consumption and electric range. It has no provisions written for bumpers, lamps or parking sensors. UN R104.scope_evidence: This Regulation applies to retro-reflective markings for vehicles of category M2, M3, N, O2, O3 and O4.

UN R116.scope_evidence: Approval of vehicle alarm systems (VAS)... Approval of immobilizers and vehicles... with regard to their devices to prevent unauthorized use

UN R148.scope_evidence: This Regulation applies to the following light-signalling devices (lamps): ... Direction indicator lamps
UN R148.reason: The bumper integrates LED front direction indicator lamps, which are a device type approved under UN R148 (front direction indicator categories 1, 1a, 1b, etc.). Front fog lamps are not in R148's scope (only rear fog lamps), so they fall under a different regulation.

UN R149.scope_evidence: This Regulation applies to the following road illumination devices (lamps): ... Front fog lamps for vehicles of categories L3, L4, L5, L7, M, N and T
UN R149.reason: The bumper integrates LED front fog lamps for an M1 vehicle, and R149 approves front fog lamps as a device type for category M. The direction indicators and other bumper functions are outside its scope.

UN R150.scope_evidence: This Regulation applies to retro-reflective devices as: • Retro-reflectors of the Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB and IVA • Retro-reflective Marking Materials ... • Advance Warning Triangles
UN R150.reason: R150 approves only retro-reflective devices, and the bumper's specification lists no retro-reflector or retro-reflective marking. Its integrated lamps (front fog lamps and direction indicators) are light-emitting devices covered by other lighting regulations, not R150.

UN R152.scope_evidence: applies to the approval of vehicles of Category M1 and N1 with regard to an on-board system to (a) Avoid or mitigate the severity of a rear-end in lane collision...
UN R152.reason: R152 approves the vehicle's Advanced Emergency Braking System, which detects collisions and brakes automatically. The bumper's ultrasonic sensors serve only low-speed parking assistance, and no AEBS radar or camera is specified, so the product does not determine AEBS performance.

wiring harness connection to vehicle electrical system

UN R161.reason: R161 covers anti-theft and immobilising devices (steering, gearbox locks, immobilisers). The front bumper's functions are impact protection, styling, lamps and parking sensors, none of which is a device to prevent unauthorized use.

UN R162.reason: The front bumper contains no immobilizer function or part, and it does not determine the vehicle's immobilizer performance. The direction indicator mention concerns only the optional use of lamps for status indication, which is not a requirement on the bumper.

UN R164.scope_evidence: This Regulation applies to new studded pneumatic tyres of Classes C1, C2 and C3 with regard to their snow performance.
UN R164.reason: R164 approves studded tyres for snow performance. The front bumper assembly contains no tyres and does not determine tyre performance, so the regulation does not apply. The 'structure' mentions refer to tyre structure, not bumper structure.

UN R171.scope_evidence: applies to the type approval of vehicles of Categories M and N2 with regard to their Driver Control Assistance Systems (DCAS)
UN R171.reason: R171 approves vehicle-level DCAS (sustained longitudinal/lateral control assistance). The direction-indicator mentions only concern the system's use of indicators during manoeuvres, and parking-assist ultrasonic sensors are not a DCAS. UN R174.scope_evidence: This Regulation applies to all seating positions in vehicles of categories M and N fitted with safety belt with regard to safety-belt reminders.
UN R174.reason: UN R174 concerns safety-belt reminder systems for seating positions. A front bumper assembly, with its lamps and parking sensors, has no role in safety-belt reminders.

UN R175.scope_evidence: applies to the type approval of vehicles of Category M1 equipped with automatic transmission with regard to their Acceleration Control for Pedal Error systems (ACPE) ... means of forward and/or rear detection
UN R175.reason: ACPE must detect obstacles 1.0–1.5 m in front of the vehicle, and front-bumper ultrasonic sensors are a typical forward detection means. If the M1 vehicle's ACPE uses these sensors, the bumper directly determines system performance. The specification does not say whether the vehicle has ACPE or an automatic transmission, or whether ACPE uses these sensors.

UN GTR 9.scope_evidence: This global technical regulation (gtr) shall apply to the frontal surfaces of power driven vehicles of category 1-1 with a gross vehicle mass exceeding 500 kg
UN GTR 9.reason: GTR 9 assesses the vehicle's frontal surfaces for pedestrian protection, with dedicated bumper provisions (bumper beam definition, bumper test area, and lower legform impact tests using the FlexPLI). The bumper's EPP energy absorber, fascia and beam directly determine the outcome of the lower-leg tests for M1 (category 1-1) vehicles.

GTR 9 is a Global Technical Regulation under the 1998 Agreement. Its pedestrian bumper/lower-leg provisions are transposed into UN R127, which is already included. Citing both would duplicate the same legform test requirements. Revisit only if a market applying GTR 9 directly (not via R127) is targeted.

UN R10.reason: The bumper contains electronic sub-assemblies fitted to an M1 vehicle: ultrasonic parking sensors, LED fog and direction indicator lamps with drivers, and the harness. R10 sets emission and immunity requirements for such ESAs, and the direction indicator is an immunity-related function.

UN R127.reason: Applies to M1 vehicles. It has bumper-specific provisions (bumper beam definition, bumper test area, lower legform impact tests), which the fascia, EPP energy absorber and beam directly determine.

UN R128.reason: R128 approves only replaceable LED light sources of the Annex 1 categories. UN R137.reason: Whole-vehicle full-width frontal crash occupant-restraint regulation with no provisions written for bumpers. The beam only indirectly influences the crash pulse, and compliance rests on the body structure and restraints.

UN R148.reason: The bumper integrates LED front direction indicator lamps, a device type approved under R148 (replaces R6). The lamps need R148 device approval: photometry, colour, markings.

UN R149.reason: The bumper integrates LED front fog lamps for an M1 vehicle. Front fog lamps are a device type approved under R149 (replaces R19).

UN R155.reason: Approves the vehicle's cyber security management system, not components. Linking ultrasonic sensors to it depends on unstated vehicle architecture, so the link is speculative. Any requirements would come via the OEM supplier agreement, not this regulation.

UN R156.reason: Approves the vehicle's software update management. The spec states no updatable firmware in the sensors or lamps, so the link is speculative.

UN R175.reason: ACPE applies only to automatic-transmission M1 vehicles equipped with ACPE. The spec does not state that the vehicle has ACPE or that these sensors serve it. The parking sensors are specified only for parking assistance, so the link is speculative.

UN R42.reason: Approves M1 front and rear protective devices (bumpers) for low-speed collision behaviour. The beam, absorber, cover and mountings directly determine the 4 km/h longitudinal and corner impact test results.

UN R94.reason: Whole-vehicle offset frontal crash occupant-protection regulation with no provisions written for bumpers. The beam's influence on the result is indirect, and compliance rests on the body structure and restraint systems.
